angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 28,981,471 km at 90.83 pc = 4.27 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 20535: distance 90.826 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.034), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 90.826 +/- 3.088 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 11.1270 +/- 0.1189 mas (same row, RUWE 2.56), 93.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 41.658 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 20535: radius 41.658 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 419.888 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.07) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 28,981,471 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4051 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 20535: effective temperature 4051 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.088) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 20535: effective temperature 4051 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.088) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 40 (BS 1393), cross-checked against Gaia DR3 XP spectrum, source 4871775051598300160 (9 levels apart at most, the threshold is 12)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.71 from 1990ApJS...74.1075M, the median of its 3 spectra; the 3 published values span log g 1.71 to 1.71, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1990ApJS...74.1075M)
